item.text: {"analysis_packet":{"certificate":"The inherited anchor is an online, standard-library policy with a legal interface and adaptive recent/frequent plus ghost-state topology, but its terminal coherence depends on reconstructing executable semantics from analysis. The candidate hypothesis supports transferring one complete executable state rather than visibility-governed re-derivation. Preserve the distinction between generative continuity and normative legality: continuity may improve coherence, but it does not excuse violations of capacity, residency, uniqueness, integer-key, online-only, or no-oracle obligations. No score or benchmark evidence is available, so performance claims remain unverified and must not be treated as facts.","witnesses":["The anchor exposes only access-time information and maintains resident byte accounting, recency/frequency partitions, ghost histories, and an adaptive recent target.","The anchor's intended behavior includes scan resistance, phase adaptation, and regret-sensitive recency/frequency balancing, but no evaluator result establishes effectiveness.","The hypothesis identifies semantic reconstruction at the terminal handoff as the bottleneck and predicts that preserving one complete executable state can retain action coherence across the handoff.","A source-class cut prevents the terminal successor from reacquiring anchor policy, hypothesis, or loop-structure evidence; therefore the successor must rely only on this synthesized analysis plus normative inputs.","Conflicts must remain explicit: inherited adaptive topology may support performance goals, while every emitted eviction must still be a currently cached unique integer key and every resulting resident state must fit capacity."],"obligations":["Emit analysis only; do not emit policy source, a patch, a diff, alternatives, rankings, or an artifact.","Preserve the required Policy constructor and access interface and use only Python standard-library facilities.","Process one access at a time using only information available online at that access; do not inspect traces, benchmark paths, reference implementations, oracle decisions, or external libraries.","Ensure returned evictions are only keys currently cached before eviction, are unique integer keys, and correspond to actual removals.","Maintain capacity safety after every request, including zero capacity, zero-size objects, repeated accesses, size changes, and objects larger than capacity.","Keep performance mechanisms subordinate to contract legality; adaptation, scan resistance, phase-shift response, and hit-rate objectives are hypotheses rather than guaranteed outcomes.","Do not infer an official score or claim validation absent evaluator evidence.","Honor the complete-state handoff principle while making all state transitions directly executable and internally coherent."],"exact_actions":["Use this packet as the sole generative synthesis available to the terminal policy authority.","Carry forward the anchor's useful distinctions—resident recency versus frequency, ghost evidence, byte accounting, and adaptive target control—only insofar as they can be implemented as a coherent online state machine.","Make the terminal artifact self-contained and executable from its own state; do not reconstruct behavior from prose or reacquire the cut sources.","For every access, normalize inputs consistently, detect resident hits before ghost handling, account for size changes, make room through actual resident removals, and return only removals made by that request.","Handle oversized requests without retaining them and without reporting unrelated or nonresident keys; preserve the cache invariant in all edge cases.","Treat ghost evidence as advisory adaptation signal, avoid admitting state that exceeds capacity, and keep all metadata from affecting returned eviction keys unless a resident key is actually removed.","Perform no score-based selection, retry, branching, or policy comparison because the topology exposes no score evidence and requires one final policy." ]},"artifact_kind":"analysis_only"}
